title: Adaptive Tempo Buckets: cadence-aware roadmap scorer for inference economics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Standard RICE scoring treats effort and impact as static inputs; for inference platform work we see strong time-to-value and capacity-regime effects (short fast wins vs long platform bets), and token-cost/latency sensitivity that varies by workload. Goal: design a practical, repeatable prioritization model that (a) augments RICE with a tempo dimension, (b) applies workload-aware multipliers for token economics and latency risk, and (c) is cycle-aware so scores decay/refresh with cadence. Deliverables: 1) Scoring rubric and spreadsheet prototype (tempo buckets: Sprint, Quarter, Strategic) combining Reach/Impact/Confidence/Effort with Tempo weight and Econ multipliers; 2) Example scoring for 12 candidate initiatives across inference, dedicated, and console; 3) Implementation guidance for PMs and Intake form changes; 4) Small pilot in next cycle to validate alignment with capacity and SLO tradeoffs. Key ideas: - Tempo buckets: Sprint (<=1 cycle, high churn tolerance), Quarter (1-3 cycles), Strategic (multi-cycle). Each bucket applies a 'tempo multiplier' that increases priority for short-window high-impact projects and reduces for long bets unless strategic signals present. - Econ multipliers: calculate expected tokens affected * estimated unit-cost delta * latency-sensitivity multiplier to produce a "cost-risk" value that reduces net impact score when negative. - Capacity regimes: tag initiatives with expected capacity regime (elastic, reserved, private) and apply scaling factors for feasibility/queueing risk. - Cycle decay: scores reduce by X% per cycle unless refreshed by new signals (customer requests, incidents, KPI regressions). Implementation notes: spreadsheet is intentionally transparent; we prefer explicit numeric multipliers and worked examples instead of black-box models. Engineering asks: need telemetry (per-route token volumes, latency cohorts) and a small simulation runner to project unit-econ impact. Success metrics: PM alignment time reduced, fewer re-prioritization meetings, and roadmap experiments delivering expected unit-econ wins in pilot cohort.
